DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN) secondary to prematurity.

The clinical picture of a 33-weeker with respiratory distress starting within 2 hours of birth, combined with the absence of maternal infection markers and the initial CXN findings, strongly points to retained fetal lung fluid. Given the lack of hypoxia or severe sepsis indicators, this fits the classic presentation of TTN.
